item.text: {"text":"Cheap ablations: hold the SASRec checkpoint, frozen embeddings, candidates, and residual-weight grid fixed; compare residual off, last-item, recent-K (e.g., 3/5/10), and full available history. Add uniformly sampled K history events and oldest-K controls; shuffling order within the same mean-pooled window changes nothing. Recent-K beating full-history and random-K supports useful recency. Compare against a training-count popularity residual, and inspect gains by target-popularity bucket and residual–popularity correlation. Cosine removes embedding-norm effects, but does not establish freedom from popularity shortcuts: [Google similarity guidance](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/recommendation/overview/candidate-generation). These are proposed controls, not established results for this augmentation.\n\nCausal implementation: at training position t, pool only nonpadding inputs through t, including the current input and excluding its next-item target; select recent-K by valid-event order, with masked counts under left padding. Full-history means the available causal prefix. [Original SASRec](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py) uses causal attention, padding masks, and the final sequence position for inference. Preserve repeated events in the main representation; ablate event-weighted versus unique-item pooling without changing input splits, and report repeat-target versus unseen-target validation slices where available. [RepeatNet](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/4408) motivates separating repeat consumption from exploration; unseen-item simulator recommendations cannot directly benefit from recommending repeats. Finally, compare diagnostic and exported candidate scores in eval mode using identical prefixes, IDs, frozen weights, normalization epsilon, residual weight, and dtype. Include short left-padded and repeated-item examples; check finite scores, numerical tolerance, rankings, and future-token invariance at earlier positions. Any mismatch invalidates the ablation comparison."}
